title: Wire vs Integuru: same network layer, different starting line
summary: Both tools skip the browser and work at the HTTP layer. Wire ships 973 pre-built sites and 5,279 actions. Integuru starts…
body_markdown:
If you're building an AI agent that needs to act on platforms without official APIs (schedule appointments in an EHR, pull shipment status from a carrier portal, submit a form in a government system), you've already worked out that browser automation doesn't scale. A headless Chromium instance per action, billing by the browser-minute, breaking on every UI redesign: the math stops working the moment you hit production volume.


Both Wire and Integuru start from the same architectural answer: skip the browser and work at the network layer. Intercept the HTTP calls the site's own frontend makes and replay them directly. Integuru advertises responses under 3 seconds and a 99.9%+ success rate; Wire's product page reports 99.95% uptime over the last 90 days. Both run at a fraction of the compute cost of a browser per action.


The Wire vs Integuru difference is how you get an integration running, and how many you can have on day one.


## How Integuru works


Integuru's hosted product is build-first. You share the website URL, provide account details if the site needs a login, and describe in natural language the data or action you want. Integuru analyzes the site's network requests and reverse-engineers the underlying API structure into a callable endpoint for exactly that workflow. Its open-source v0 shows the method in the open: a HAR file of browser requests goes in, a dependency graph of upstream requests is traced, and runnable code comes out.


The result is a production API that makes direct HTTP requests: no browser, no RPA, no frontend dependency. On the Production plan, auth auto-healing and a 24/7 on-call team update integrations when they need attention.


Integuru says[most APIs are generated within 20 minutes](https://www.integuru.com/faq) .


For teams that don't want to manage this themselves, Integuru offers a fully managed service with custom pricing: you specify the platforms and workflows, and they build and maintain everything end to end.


Their open-source v0 ([about 4.7K GitHub stars](https://github.com/Integuru-AI/Integuru) , AGPL-3.0) is public if you want to inspect the dependency-graph approach before committing.


## How Wire works


Wire's starting point is different: a pre-built catalog.


973 sites. 5,279 actions, as of 25 October 2026. Finance portals, marketplaces, government systems, e-commerce platforms, travel, research databases: all available immediately, behind a single API key, with no setup required. You browse the catalog, pick the action, and[submit a task](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/wire/execute-task) .


```text
# Submit
curl -X POST https://api.anakin.io/v1/wire/task \
-H "X-API-Key: $ANAKIN_API_KEY" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{"action_id": "am_search_products", "params": {"query": "noise cancelling headphones"}}'
# returns {"job_id": "...", "status": "processing", "poll_url": "..."}


# Poll
curl https://api.anakin.io/v1/wire/jobs/{job_id} \
-H "X-API-Key: $ANAKIN_API_KEY"
# returns {"status": "completed", "result": {...}}
```


For any platform outside the catalog, you[submit a build request](https://anakin.io/docs/api-reference/wire/create-build-request) with the site URL and a plain-English goal. Wire's builder generates the action, auto-tests it against the live site, and publishes it to the catalog on success. Most new sites ship within days.


For enterprise internal portals, the custom systems that will never appear in a public catalog, Wire also offers managed integration services: you specify the platform, requirements, and expected volume, and Wire's team builds and maintains the integration.


Wire maintains every integration it ships. When a target site changes its internal request signatures, Wire re-detects and updates the endpoint. The action_id values your code calls stay stable, so nothing changes on your side when a site's internals shift.


Credentials never travel in request payloads. Wire's AES-256 named identity vault stores them at rest; your agent passes an identity reference at runtime, and Wire resolves actual credentials server-side.

## The breadth gap


Integuru's pricing shows how it thinks about coverage. The Production plan[starts at $499 per month](https://www.integuru.com/) for one platform and 10,000 API calls, and each additional platform is another $499 per month. If you need integrations with 10 platforms, that's $499 base plus $4,491 in platform add-ons: $4,990 per month before extra accounts or call volume. Each of those platforms is also a separate integration to generate before it can be called.


Wire's catalog flips the math. The 973 sites in the catalog cost nothing extra to access; they're included under a single key. For teams building agents that need to act across many platforms (search Amazon, pull a LinkedIn profile, file a government form, check a shipping status), the catalog means those capabilities are available before you write a single line of agent logic.


The gap widens for agents that act across many platforms at once. Integuru's per-platform pricing and per-platform build scale linearly with breadth. Wire's catalog scales to platform count without additional setup or platform fees.


## Where Integuru has a genuine edge


For deeply custom enterprise portals (internal ERP systems, proprietary healthcare platforms, bespoke logistics software that no general catalog will ever cover), Integuru's build-per-platform model can be a precise fit. The integration is generated from your exact system's own network requests, not inferred from a generic template.


Their open-source v0 also gives engineering teams a way to inspect the approach before committing to a production contract, and that transparency is a real point in its favor.


For healthcare specifically, Integuru states it is HIPAA-compliant and signs BAAs at no additional cost, which can make procurement faster. Wire is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 certified, which covers most enterprise and regulated-industry requirements, but teams whose compliance checklist leads with HIPAA will want to weigh Integuru's position there.


## When Wire is the better fit


Wire is the faster path when:


- The platforms you need are already in the catalog: Amazon, GitHub, Shopify, Reddit, Zillow, and more than 960 others are available immediately
- You're building a broad agent that acts across many platforms and don't want to pay per platform or wait on a new build for each one
- You want one API key and one billing line across every site your agent touches, with credits refunded when a job fails
- You need ISO 27001:2022 in addition to SOC 2 Type II
- You want[MCP integration](https://anakin.io/docs/integrations/ai-agents/mcp-server) for Claude, Cursor, or Cline out of the box


Wire is also the answer when the workflow already exists somewhere in the catalog and you want it running in the next 10 minutes, not after a per-platform build and a new monthly add-on.


## Pricing in practice


Integuru's add-on pricing ($499 per platform per month) is transparent and predictable for single-platform use cases. For multi-platform agents, the cost compounds quickly: 5 platforms on Production is $499 base plus $1,996 in platform add-ons, $2,495 per month before call volume.


Wire bills per call in credits, with no platform fees and no per-workflow setup. Simple read actions such as Amazon product search cost 1 credit, and the Wire product page puts the cost at $0.001 per call. At that rate, an agent calling 10 platforms 1,000 times each pays about $10. Every account starts with[300 free credits](https://anakin.io/pricing) , and the economics favour breadth: more platforms doesn't mean a higher monthly floor.


## The call


Both Wire and Integuru got the architecture right. The browser is overhead that doesn't belong in your agent's runtime path; HTTP is the right layer.


What's different is what you start with. Integuru starts from zero and builds up one generated integration at a time. Wire starts with 973 sites and 5,279 pre-built actions, and adds new ones (catalog, build request, or managed) without a per-platform fee.


If your agent needs to act on platforms that exist in Wire's catalog, those actions are available now. If you're building into custom internal systems that no catalog will ever cover, Wire's managed service and Integuru's build-per-platform model are both viable paths.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the main difference between Wire and Integuru?


Both work at the network layer and call the HTTP requests a site's own frontend makes, with no browser in the loop. Wire starts with a pre-built catalog of 973 sites and 5,279 actions (as of 25 October 2026) under one API key. Integuru starts from zero and generates an integration for each platform you request.


### How does Integuru build an integration?


On its hosted product, you share the website URL, provide account details if a login is needed, and describe the workflow in natural language. Integuru analyzes the site's network requests and generates an API; it says most APIs are generated within 20 minutes. Its open-source v0 builds the same kind of dependency graph from a HAR file.


### How much does Integuru cost compared with Wire?


Integuru has a free plan, a Production plan that starts at $499 per month for one platform and 10,000 API calls, $499 per month for each additional platform, and a custom-priced managed service. Wire has no platform fee: it bills credits per call (Amazon product search costs 1 credit), and every account starts with 300 free credits.


### What happens if a site is not in Wire's catalog?


You submit a build request with the site URL and a plain-English goal. Wire's builder generates the action, auto-tests it against the live site and publishes it on success; most new sites ship within days. For internal enterprise portals, Wire also offers a managed integration service.


### Which tool fits HIPAA-led healthcare procurement?


Integuru states it is HIPAA-compliant and signs BAAs at no additional cost. Wire is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 certified, which covers most enterprise and regulated-industry requirements.
